study: Name history: does a stock's OWN recent history - whether it tends to trend (follow through after new highs) or snap back - and its higher-timeframe trend (15-min structure, 60-min trend) predict whether a new intraday high keeps going? And (information) does a multi-day key level nearby matter?
registered_at: 2026-10-08 ~12:00 ET (commit f9df947); amended ~12:40 ET before any script or data
origin: Operator 10/8: 'higher highs and lower lows - have we looked at the history of the name, not just the current market data'; 'should we look at 15m timeframes for our entries and the 1hr timeframe for clear uptrends'; 'do we need a helper to look at the entirety of the day history of the name to find a key level for confluence'. Every entry test so far used today's data; the only multi-day facts used were daily context (gap, 50-day MA, news), which picked NAMES, not minutes.
prior: LOW to MODERATE. Against: multi-timeframe EMA alignment on 1/5/10m failed (STRATEGY_EDGE_ROUND2 test 6: no better than random in the same name-hour); stock-level intraday persistence is usually weak; S/R levels (10/2) and breakouts (10/6 history) failed. For: name selection is the only place effects appeared (needle study, daily context); per-name trendiness and 15m/60m structure are untested.
universe: point-in-time each session D: the top 400 names by RAW SIP close x volume on D-1 over the bro_sr_wr asset set (active and inactive US common stock; no ETF/ETP/levered), with raw SIP close on D-1 >= $10. Top-400 names with no bars at all on D are logged separately from fetch failures.
data: SIP 1-minute and daily bars (Alpaca historical), 04:00-16:00 ET. RAW prices (adjustment=raw) for the universe, the event, the prior close, LEVELS and costs; split/dividend-ADJUSTED prices only for look-back features (T1, T2, T3, EMA); a name-day with a split inside its 20-session look-back is dropped (counted). Sessions 2026-05-26 .. 2026-10-07: first 20 look-back only, ~74 test sessions. SIP NBBO quotes at each event and control. After hours only; requests and failures recorded; abort if > 2% of name-days fail.
event: per name per test session D, the FIRST 1-minute bar t with 10:30 <= bar close time <= 15:00 ET such that (a) close(t) >= 1.001 x max(high of RTH bars 09:30 .. t-1) (bar t's own high and premarket excluded), and (b) max(high of RTH bars 09:30..t) >= 1.005 x prior close (prior close = raw SIP daily close of D-1). Entry at the SIP NBBO mid at t + 5 s; exits at the mid at entry + 30 min (net30) and + 15 min (net15, information); cost = half the full spread at entry + half at exit; quotes must be <= 5 s old, else the event is dropped and counted (drop rates reported per group; if the groups' drop rates differ by > 2 percentage points the run is flagged FAILED-DATA and not read).

features_known_at_t.T1_hh_followthrough: over the prior 20 sessions (adjusted bars), for each session's first event defined as above: SUCCESS if a later bar's high > event close x 1.001 within 30 min BEFORE any bar's low <= event close x 0.997; a bar that does both counts as FAILURE; neither within 30 min = FAILURE (windows end by 15:30). T1 = success share; >= 8 events required, else missing
features_known_at_t.T2_autocorr15: over the prior 20 sessions, lag-1 correlation of consecutive non-overlapping 15-minute RTH returns (09:30-16:00, within-session pairs only)
features_known_at_t.TREND_SCORE: mean of the cross-sectional percentile ranks of T1 and T2 among that session's events (both required)
features_known_at_t.HTF_UP: at t: the 3 most recent COMPLETED 15-min RTH bars (aligned to 09:30, completed = bar end <= t) B1<B2<B3 satisfy high(B2) > high(B1), high(B3) > high(B2), low(B2) > low(B1), low(B3) > low(B2) (2 comparisons each); AND the last completed 60-min RTH bar (09:30-10:30, 10:30-11:30, ...; the 15:30-16:00 half bar is its own bar on prior days) has close > EMA20 of 60-min closes and EMA20 > EMA20 three bars earlier; EMA seeded at the first look-back bar (>= 20 sessions x 7 bars of warm-up)
features_known_at_t.T3_trend_day_share: information: share of the prior 20 sessions with |close - open| / (high - low) >= 0.6
features_known_at_t.LEVELS_info: information (the 'confluence helper'): multi-day key levels known at t - prior 5 sessions' highs and lows, prior close, today's premarket high, 20-session high, and round numbers ($1 steps under $50, $5 above) - distance from t's close to the nearest level above, and the count of levels within 0.20% above (confluence)

hypotheses.H1: events in the TOP tercile of TREND_SCORE minus events in the BOTTOM tercile: net30 difference > 0
hypotheses.H2: events with HTF_UP true minus HTF_UP false: net30 difference > 0

statistic: PRIMARY outcome = HEDGED net30 = net30 - beta x SPY return over the same 30 min (beta = OLS of the name's 1-min-bar 30-min returns on SPY's over the prior 20 sessions, point-in-time). For each hypothesis: difference in mean hedged net30 between groups, OLS with session fixed effects AND event-hour fixed effects, TWO-WAY clustered SE (session and name); distinct names per group reported. Raw net30 reported alongside. Halves = alternate test sessions (calendar order).
power: before any mean: n events and distinct names per group per half and the two-way SE; MDE = (t_crit + 0.84) x SE. UNDERPOWERED only if MDE > 10 bp; if MDE <= 10 bp in both halves and the pass is not met, the verdict is FAIL
pass: per hypothesis (Bonferroni 2, one-sided: t_crit = the 2.24 equivalent at the smaller cluster df): hedged difference >= +5 bp with two-way t >= t_crit pooled, same sign in both halves, the better group's HEDGED net30 > 0 after costs, AND still > 0 after dropping the 5 names and (separately) the 3 sessions with the largest share of the difference (share = that unit's summed contribution to the group-mean difference). FAIL if pooled two-way t <= -2, or as in 'power'. Otherwise UNDERPOWERED. A historical PASS is labelled 'NAME SELECTION' (not an entry signal) unless the same-name control cell (information_only #1) is also positive; and it must be RERUN with the same code on >= 60 earlier sessions (2025-11 onward) AND on IEX bars before any forward test on the desk is pre-registered. No information cell can be promoted.
information_only: SAME-NAME CONTROL: for each top-tercile (H1) and HTF_UP (H2) event, a random minute (seed 61) in the same name, session and clock hour, not within 30 min of the event, same entry/exit/cost; event minus control (entry-signal vs name-selection test)
H2 on the H1-eligible subset (names with T1 defined); T1-missing rate per H2 group and per session
corr(TREND_SCORE, HTF_UP); H1 within each HTF_UP stratum
terciles of 20-day realized volatility (T2/T3 may proxy volatility); H1 and H2 within volatility terciles
LEVELS_info: hedged net30 by nearest-level distance band (< 0.2%, 0.2-0.5%, > 0.5%, none) and confluence count (0, 1, >= 2)
short mirror (new session LOW on a down day) for H1
TREND_SCORE stability: month-to-month rank correlation per name; T2 sampling-noise estimate (SE ~ 1/sqrt(pairs))
no_retuning: the event, the 20-session look-back, the T1/T2 definitions, terciles, the 15m/60m rule, the 30-min hold and the bar are fixed here
tool: tools/studies/name_history.py (to be written; skeptic code review before it scores anything)
caveats: SIP history vs the desk's live IEX feed (the event uses consolidated bars; the desk would see IEX)
the event is a breakout-style new high, not the desk's %R square; a pass speaks to 'higher highs on trending names', and the desk version is a separate forward test
70 test sessions in one market regime (Sep-Oct 2026 up-trending tape)
